43.diagnosis: Strict 7-step diagnosis of champion Exp 6 (XGBoost test_auc=0.5414). Per-prediction analysis on the 30,222 test rows reveals catastrophic recall failure: TP=76, FN=1313 (recall=0.0547), with FN confidence mean=0.907 vs TP confidence mean=0.173. The model is overconfidently predicting CLEAN on actual fraud rows. Threshold-sensitivity analysis shows the failure is structural (varying threshold from 0.1 to 0.6 yields F1 in [0, 0.089]) — there is no decision threshold that rescues recall. Root cause: XGBoost was trained on imbalanced data (train fraud rate=11.4%) with default scale_pos_weight=1, so the gradient signal heavily favors the 88.6% majority class. The model learned to predict CLEAN for almost everything; the 0.5414 test AUC is preserved only because the few positive predictions are still slightly better-ranked than random.
43.citations:
Pozzolo, Caelen, Johnson & Bontempi 2015 IEEE-SSCI 'Calibrating Probability with Undersampling for Unbalanced Classification' — establishes that imbalanced binary classification requires either re-sampling or class-weighted loss; for tree boosting, scale_pos_weight = N_neg/N_pos is the standard correction because it rebalances the per-example gradient contribution without changing the data distribution.;
King & Zeng 2001 Political Analysis 'Logistic Regression in Rare Events Data' (DOI:10.1093/pan/9.2.137) — formalizes that for rare-event detection (fraud rate < 15%), models trained without prior correction systematically underestimate the positive class probability, yielding low recall even when AUC is moderate; this exactly matches the Exp 6 failure pattern observed in the diagnostic. Both papers motivate setting scale_pos_weight ≈ 7.8 for our 11.4% train fraud rate.
43.hypothesis: We hypothesize that setting scale_pos_weight=8.0 on the Exp 6 XGBoost config (single-axis change, all other HPs identical) will lift test AUC into the 0.55 to 0.62 range and recall from 0.055 to >0.30 because the mechanism per Pozzolo et al. 2015 is that the per-example gradient magnitude on positive (fraud) rows is multiplied by 8, forcing the second-order tree-boosting objective to find splits that separate the positive class even at the cost of slightly higher false positives; the AUC improvement comes from probabilities being less collapsed near 0, giving more separation between fraud and clean rankings.
43.prediction: Test AUC-ROC should land in the range 0.55 to 0.62, decisively beating Exp 6's 0.5414. Recall should improve from 0.0547 to between 0.30 and 0.50. F1 should improve from 0.088 to 0.20-0.30. Val AUC expected to track test AUC within ±0.01. If AUC reaches 0.60+ this is the largest single-experiment gain since Exp 2 baseline and validates the rare-events-correction diagnosis; if AUC stays below 0.55, scale_pos_weight is not the binding constraint and the next experiment must explore focal loss or undersampling.
